poetry--agent--webmcp.doc:
The registrar: one controller on an opted-in component root (`webmcp: "country"` on the helper call renders it beside the component's own controllers) registers that instance's declared tools with document.modelContext on connect and aborts them on disconnect. Components gain zero runtime code - each tool dispatches to the component's OWN controller action (the `executes` descriptor the Ruby contract validated at class load), passing the tool's parameters positionally in declared order.

Correctness rules the spec makes load-bearing: - Re-registration is skipped while the payload is unchanged (the spec documents an unregister/quick-re-register race where in-flight args for the old tool can hit the new tool's schema). - Never register under Turbo's cache preview. - Duplicate names are rejected by the browser; we warn and skip. - A per-document budget caps registrations (each tool costs the agent context; overlap confuses tool choice). - Errors come back as descriptive result strings (granular exceptions are still open spec issues; a string lets the agent self-correct): a missing or unknown parameter, a value of the wrong type or outside the enum, a missing action, a throwing action. - A result is the action's return value when it is JSON-serializable (the contract's actions return their resulting state, so an answer says what happened rather than "done"); the done marker covers actions that return nothing. - Parameters map positionally onto the action in declared order; the execute callback's {signal} is not forwarded (the actions are synchronous UI operations).

name.doc: The instance name the tools register under (poetry.<name>.<tool>).

tools.doc: The tool definitions this instance registers, as the component declared them.

budget.doc: The most tools one page registers; past it, further registrations are dropped with a console warning.

method_docs.connect: Registers this instance's tools and records it for the executor.
method_docs.disconnect: Forgets the instance and aborts its registrations.
method_docs.execute: Runs one of this instance's tools by its registered or short name; an unknown name resolves to an error message.
method_docs.register: Registers every declared tool with the browser under the instance name, within the page budget; skipped when unsupported or in a preview.
method_docs.unregister: Aborts every registration of this instance and announces it.

poetry--agent--webmcp-form.doc:
The declarative-form companion: a form declared with poetry_webmcp_form (toolname/tooldescription on the <form>) is registered by the BROWSER; this controller only answers an agent-invoked submit with the outcome. Chrome's SubmitEvent carries agentInvoked + respondWith(promise): we submit the form ourselves (fetch, same method/action, Turbo-Stream accepting) and respond with a short descriptive result instead of navigating, so the agent learns whether the submission succeeded and what the server said (validation errors included - it can self-correct).

The person's page then catches up with the answer (a beat after the result is handed to the browser, so a navigation can never swallow it): a GET answer is the page at that URL - a Turbo visit, or a plain navigation without Turbo; a Turbo-Stream answer renders; a redirected POST (redirect-after-create) visits where the redirect went. An HTML re-render of a failed POST stays put - the agent already holds the errors, and the person keeps their filled form.

Submits without agentInvoked (a person pressed Submit) pass through untouched: the human path stays the human path.

method_docs.disconnect: Stops listening for the form's submit.

poetry--agent--agui-client-tool.doc: The AG-UI client-tool bridge: the relay appends one of these per tool call the agent made to a FRONTEND tool - a component tool the page declared - and this controller executes it through the registrar (the same dispatch a WebMCP call takes, so it works in every browser, modelContext or not), then POSTs the result to the continue URL. The server folds the tool message into the transcript and answers with the next run's streams, which Turbo renders. A tool declared to ask first renders the host's approval prompt inside the element and waits: its approve action runs the call, its deny action answers it as declined without running it, and either answer hides the prompt. One element, one answer: the done flag makes a Turbo re-render inert.

call.doc: The pending tool call: its id, name and arguments.

url.doc: Where the tool result is posted.

done.doc: Whether the call has already been answered (a restored snapshot must not answer twice).

confirm.doc: Whether the call waits for the user's approve or deny before anything runs.

method_docs.approve: Runs the call the user approved.
method_docs.connect: Runs the pending client tool once, unless it waits for the user.
method_docs.deny: Answers the call as declined: the tool never runs, and the agent is told so.

poetry--agent--a2ui-surface.doc:
The client side of an A2UI surface's checks: the server renders the program (every checked component's rules, spelled as v1.0 spells them whatever the surface speaks: `{"@path"}` bindings made absolute, `{"@call", args}` calls, a literal `@` key doubled; the path each checked control binds; the bound inputs by path with their kinds; and the data model) and this controller evaluates it as the user types.

A button whose own checks fail is disabled from the start. What the user sees of a failure waits for them: an input's message and invalid state appear once its path has been edited, a button's reason once any input has. Until then the server's rendering stands, including the failures it rendered after a rejected action; one the browser cannot judge (a rule on a function it does not know) stands until the server judges it again. A morph keeps the element and this controller, so the edited inputs are judged again once the morph is over.

The five validators and the three combinators are the checks vocabulary; anything else passes here and is judged by the server, which re-runs every rule on the action.

program.doc: The check program the server compiled: the checks (each with the path its control binds), the bound inputs by path, and the data model.

method_docs.apply: Reflects a check's verdict on the elements bound to a key. A button disables while its checks fail. The message and the invalid state follow the verdict only once the user has touched the input (any input, for a button); before that, and for a server failure the browser cannot judge, the server's rendering stands.
method_docs.call: Runs a catalog function by name with its arguments resolved; an unknown name resolves to null.
method_docs.evaluate: Runs every check in the program and applies its failures.
method_docs.failure: A rule's failure message, null when it passes, or undefined when it cannot be decided here.
method_docs.initialize: Starts with nothing touched: the paths the user has edited since the surface mounted.
method_docs.morphed: Evaluates every check once a morph of the surface is over: the morph left the slots and attributes as the server rendered them, and the edited inputs keep their values. One pass per morph, however many elements it touched.
method_docs.read: The current value of a bound path from the form's inputs, falling back to the data model.
method_docs.resolve: A value with its bindings read and its calls run, recursively; a literal object's doubled `@@` keys read as their literal.
method_docs.touch: Marks the edited input's path touched and evaluates every check.

poetry--agent--mcp-app-host.doc:
The frame another server's MCP App renders in, and the host's half of the bridge. The element carries the call (server, tool, input, result, the app's resource) and where the sandbox page and the RPC endpoint are; the controller reads the app's HTML through the endpoint, mounts the sandbox proxy frame (on the apps origin, or as an opaque frame of the page's own in the inline mode), answers `ui/initialize` with the page's theme and tokens, delivers the input and the result, sends the app's own requests to the endpoint, resizes to what the app reports, and tears the app down when the element leaves.

What the page hears: `poetry:mcp-app-host:connect` (the app's info), `poetry:mcp-app-host:message` (a message for the chat, `detail.params`), `poetry:mcp-app-host:context` (a model-context update), and `poetry:mcp-app-host:display-mode` (a request; the handler may set `detail.mode` to grant one; `inline` otherwise), and with `debug`, `poetry:mcp-app-host:trace` for every message both ways. A link is opened in a new tab after the person confirms it.

server.doc: The server's id in the host's registry.

tool.doc: The tool the app belongs to.

result.doc: The tool's result (a CallToolResult), as JSON.

rpcUrl.doc: Where the app's own requests go: a POST taking { server, method, params }.

sandboxUrl.doc: The sandbox page's URL on the apps origin; absent in the inline mode.

sandboxOrigin.doc: The apps origin, the only origin the frame's messages are accepted from.

sandboxPage.doc: The sandbox page's HTML for the inline mode, written into an opaque frame of the page's own.

height.doc: The frame's height before the app reports its size, in pixels.

maxHeight.doc: The most the frame grows to, in pixels.

debug.doc: Whether every message both ways is announced as a `poetry:mcp-app-host:trace` event, for a log.

method_docs.connect: Mounts the frame and starts the handshake.
method_docs.disconnect: Tears the app down and removes the frame.
method_docs.emit: Dispatches a page event under the controller's prefix.
method_docs.hostContext: The host context the app is initialized with.
method_docs.initialized: Once the app is initialized: tells the page, delivers the input and the result.
method_docs.mount: Reads the app's HTML through the endpoint, builds the bridge and the frame, and starts the sandbox.
method_docs.openLink: Opens a link the app asks for, in a new tab, after the person confirms it.
method_docs.post: Posts a message to the frame, to the apps origin only.
method_docs.receive: Takes a message from the frame: the proxy's ready note gets the app's HTML, everything else goes to the bridge.
method_docs.resize: Sizes the frame to what the app reports: the height within the cap, the width as a floor that still shrinks with the container.
method_docs.rpc: Sends one of the app's requests to the endpoint.
method_docs.status: Shows a status line, when the element has one.
method_docs.themeChanged: Tells the app the page's theme and tokens changed.
method_docs.unmount: Asks the app to tear down, drops the bridge and removes the frame.
